verses.verse:
कृष्णा तु निर्माता कृष्णै र्गीताकारैः सुयोगिभिः।
प्रारम्भे कष्टसाध्या सा परिणामें तु सुखप्रदा।३९।
verses.text: The Kṛṣṇā was made by Kṛṣṇa, the author of the Gītā and the great yogī; at the start it is hard to master, but in the end it gives joy.

commentary.text: That is, the Kṛṣṇā flute was made by Lord Yogeśvara Śrī Kṛṣṇa. So it has only this much fault, that at the start one has to practise it with hardship, and so some people grow weary of this hardship and give it up. But having got past that hardship, those sādhakas (practitioners) become all the happier. Merits: (1) Children think it useless and leave it alone. (2) It is not jūṭhā (defiled by the mouth). (3) With the practice of breath and lips its tone grows ever sweeter. Merit (4): This flute can be made with one's own hands. Not many tools are needed to make it: bring a bamboo or a PVC pipe from the market, close one end with a cork or rubber, mark the places of the holes and make the holes, even with the point of a pair of scissors, and the flute will be ready. (5) Depending on one's blowing, this flute can be played from the softest to the loudest sound, which is called volume; this comes easily in it. (6) If needed for an ensemble, it can be raised or lowered by the blowing to match. (So the Kṛṣṇā flute, having these many merits, is the best of all. Now let us look at the merits and faults of the prākṛtika (natural) flute.)
